subject: math
title: Area and Perimeter Formulas
seo_title: Grade 4 Area and Perimeter Worksheets: Formulas, Unknown Sides, L-Shapes and Word Problems
standard_text: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems. For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 area and perimeter worksheets: use A = l × w and P = 2l + 2w, find an unknown side from the area or perimeter, choose area or perimeter, squares, L-shapes and real-world word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Area = length × width. Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width.
key_sub: Area covers the inside and is in square units (sq ft). Perimeter goes around the edge and is a length (ft). To find a missing side, divide the area by the side you know.
body_html:
Two different questions

Area is the space inside a shape, measured in square units (sq ft, sq m). Perimeter is the distance around it, measured in units of length (ft, m). For a rectangle, each one has a formula.

The two formulas

A = l × w    P = 2 × l + 2 × w (or 2 × (l + w))

Example

A rectangle is 24 m long and 15 m wide. Find the area and the perimeter.

A = 24 × 15 = 360 (24 × 10 = 240, 24 × 5 = 120, 240 + 120 = 360). P = 2 × 24 + 2 × 15 = 48 + 30 = 78.

Answer: 360 sq m and 78 m

Find an unknown side

The area formula is a multiplication with a missing factor. Divide the area by the side you know.

From the perimeter

A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 m. It is 15 m long. How wide is it?

Two lengths: 2 × 15 = 30. 50 − 30 = 20 for the two widths. 20 ÷ 2 = 10.

Answer: 10 m

Area or perimeter?

The jobFindUnit
Carpet, tiles, paint, grassArea (cover the inside)sq ft, sq m
Fence, border, ribbon, trimPerimeter (go around the edge)ft, m, in

L-shapes

Split the shape into two rectangles and add their areas. Or find the big rectangle and subtract the missing corner.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
P = l × w (12 × 5 = 60 ft)Perimeter adds all 4 sides: 2 × 12 + 2 × 5 = 34 ft
Adding only two sides (12 + 5 = 17)A rectangle has 4 sides. Double the sum: 34
Writing ft for an areaArea is square units: 60 sq ft
Perimeter 50, length 15: 50 − 15 = 35Take away both lengths, then halve: (50 − 30) ÷ 2 = 10
L-shape area = big rectangle (11 × 9 = 99)Subtract the cut-out corner: 99 − 24 = 75

faq.q: What are the area and perimeter formulas for a rectangle?
faq.a: Area = length × width (A = l × w), in square units. Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width (P = 2l + 2w), in units of length.

faq.q: How do you find the missing side of a rectangle when you know the area?
faq.a: Divide the area by the side you know. If the area is 72 sq ft and the length is 9 ft, the width is 72 ÷ 9 = 8 ft.

faq.q: How do you know whether a word problem is asking for area or perimeter?
faq.a: If something covers the inside (carpet, tiles, paint, grass), find the area. If something goes around the edge (fence, border, ribbon, trim), find the perimeter.
It is the Common Core Grade 4 standard for using the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and math problems, including finding an unknown side length from the area or perimeter.

items.q: A farmer puts a fence around a field that is 48 meters long and 17 meters wide. Which equation finds the length of the fence?

items.q: A park plants grass on a lawn that is 27 meters long and 15 meters wide. Which equation finds the area of grass?

items.q: A rectangle is 32 m long and 25 m wide. What is its perimeter?

items.q: A family buys carpet for a floor that is 27 feet long and 19 feet wide. Which equation finds how much carpet covers the floor?

items.q: A rectangle is 38 cm long and 24 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 38 × 24 = 912 sq cm (38 × 20 = 760, 38 × 4 = 152, 760 + 152 = 912). Multiply every part: 38 × 24 is not only 30 × 20 plus 8 × 4.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 18 + 2 × 12 = 36 + 24 = 60 ft. Or add first: 18 + 12 = 30, then 2 × 30 = 60 ft.

items.q: A rectangle is 38 in long and 25 in wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 38 × 25 = 950 sq in (38 × 20 = 760, 38 × 5 = 190, 760 + 190 = 950). Multiply every part: 38 × 25 is not only 30 × 20 plus 8 × 5.

items.q: The area of the rectangle is 60 sq cm. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 10 × ? = 60. 60 ÷ 10 = 6, so the side is 6 cm. Check: 10 × 6 = 60.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 50 in. What is the width marked ?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 15 = 30. 50 − 30 = 20 for the two widths, so each width is 20 ÷ 2 = 10 in. Check: 15 + 10 + 15 + 10 = 50.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 64 ft. It is 21 ft long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 21 = 42. 64 − 42 = 22 for the two widths, so each width is 22 ÷ 2 = 11 ft. Check: 21 + 11 + 21 + 11 = 64.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 108 sq in. Its length is 9 in. What is its width?
items.e: Think of the area formula with a missing factor: 9 × ? = 108. Divide: 108 ÷ 9 = 12 in. Check: 9 × 12 = 108.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 m. It is 10 m long. Which equation can you use to find the width, w?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width, so 2 × 10 + 2 × w = 36. 20 + 2 × w = 36, 2 × w = 16, w = 8 m.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 44 ft. What is the width marked ?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 14 = 28. 44 − 28 = 16 for the two widths, so each width is 16 ÷ 2 = 8 ft. Check: 14 + 8 + 14 + 8 = 44.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 126 sq ft. Its length is 7 ft. What is its width?

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 26 ft. It is 7 ft long. Which equation can you use to find the width, w?

items.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm. Check: 4 × 25 = 100. (10 × 10 = 100 is an area, not a perimeter.)

items.q: This is a piece of cardboard cut for a model. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all 6 sides: 5 + 3 + 6 + 4 + 11 + 7 = 36 cm. Do not skip the two short sides at the cut-out corner.

items.q: Mia puts ribbon around the edge of a poster that is 36 inches tall and 24 inches wide. How much ribbon does she need?
items.e: Ribbon goes around the edge, so find the perimeter: 2 × 36 + 2 × 24 = 72 + 48 = 120 inches. (864 sq in is the area of the poster.)

items.q: This is the shape of a skate park. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all 6 sides: 7 + 5 + 6 + 4 + 13 + 9 = 44 m. Do not skip the two short sides at the cut-out corner.

items.q: This is the floor plan of a kitchen. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: The two shorter sides going across, ? and 8 ft, together match the long 15 ft side. 15 − 8 = 7 ft.

items.q: A rectangular dog park has an area of 240 square meters. It is 20 meters long. How many meters of fence go around the park?
items.e: Step 1: width = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 m. Step 2: perimeter = 2 × 20 + 2 × 12 = 40 + 24 = 64 m. (12 m is only the width, not the fence.)

items.q: This is the shape of a patio. The dashed line splits it into two rectangles. What is its area?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 7 = 56 and 6 × 4 = 24. Add: 56 + 24 = 80 sq ft. Check: big rectangle 14 × 7 = 98, minus the cut-out corner 6 × 3 = 18: 98 − 18 = 80 sq ft.

items.q: This is the shape of a swimming area at a lake. Think of a 14 by 7 rectangle with a corner cut out. What is its area?
items.e: Big rectangle 14 × 7 = 98, minus the cut-out corner 8 × 3 = 24: 98 − 24 = 74 sq m. Check: split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 8 × 4 = 32. Add: 42 + 32 = 74 sq m.

items.q: A school playground is 45 meters long and 32 meters wide. What is its area?
This is the floor plan of a room. The dashed line splits it into two rectangles. What is its area?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 5 × 9 = 45 and 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 45 + 28 = 73 sq ft. Check: big rectangle 12 × 9 = 108, minus the cut-out corner 7 × 5 = 35: 108 − 35 = 73 sq ft.

items.q: Ava's backyard is 30 feet long and 20 feet wide. A patio that is 10 feet by 8 feet is in the yard. The rest is grass. What is the area of the grass?
items.e: Whole yard: 30 × 20 = 600 sq ft. Patio: 10 × 8 = 80 sq ft. Grass: 600 − 80 = 520 sq ft.

items.q: This is the shape of an L-shaped garden. Think of a 13 by 7 rectangle with a corner cut out. What is its area?
items.e: Big rectangle 13 × 7 = 91, minus the cut-out corner 6 × 3 = 18: 91 − 18 = 73 sq m. Check: split it into two rectangles: 7 × 7 = 49 and 6 × 4 = 24. Add: 49 + 24 = 73 sq m.

items.q: A coach runs around a rectangular field 2 times. The field is 90 meters long and 60 meters wide. How far does the coach run?
items.e: Once around: 2 × 90 + 2 × 60 = 300 m. Two times around: 2 × 300 = 600 m.

items.q: Leo builds a fence around a rectangular garden that is 18 meters long and 11 meters wide. How many meters of fence does he need?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 18 + 2 × 11 = 36 + 22 = 58 m. The fence goes along all 4 sides.

items.q: Lily covers a laundry room floor that is 9 feet by 8 feet with square tiles. Each tile is 1 square foot and costs $3. How much do the tiles cost?
items.e: Step 1: area = 9 × 8 = 72 sq ft, so 72 tiles. Step 2: cost = 72 × $3 = $216.

items.q: A rectangular bedroom has 132 square feet of flooring. The room is 12 feet long. How wide is the room?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 12 × ? = 132. 132 ÷ 12 = 11. The room is 11 feet wide.

items.q: This is the shape of a wooden deck. The dashed line splits it into two rectangles. What is its area?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 5 × 9 = 45 and 7 × 5 = 35. Add: 45 + 35 = 80 sq ft. Check: big rectangle 12 × 9 = 108, minus the cut-out corner 7 × 4 = 28: 108 − 28 = 80 sq ft.

items.q: Nora's room is 14 feet long and 11 feet wide. She puts baseboard along the bottom of every wall, except for a doorway that is 3 feet wide. How much baseboard does she need?
items.e: Perimeter: 2 × 14 + 2 × 11 = 50 ft. No baseboard goes across the doorway: 50 − 3 = 47 ft.

items.q: Jack used 86 feet of fence to go around a rectangular garden. The garden is 25 feet long. How wide is it?
items.e: Two lengths: 2 × 25 = 50. 86 − 50 = 36 for the two widths. 36 ÷ 2 = 18 ft.

items.q: A swimming pool is 25 meters long and 12 meters wide. A cover goes over the whole pool. What is the area of the cover?
items.e: Area = length × width = 25 × 12 = 300 sq m (25 × 10 = 250, 25 × 2 = 50, 250 + 50 = 300). The cover spreads over the whole surface, so this is area.

items.q: A soccer field is 100 meters long and 64 meters wide. What is the area of the field?
items.e: Area = 100 × 64 = 6,400 sq m. Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros after 64.
